messages:
Alex: I’m taking the night handoff now — quick summary: ongoing latency spike affecting inference.rwsvc (p99 increased from 120ms -> ~900ms). Alerting: page on call (several customer-facing 5xxs reported).
Alex: Current ownership: primary=Alex (me), secondary=Priya, comms=Jordan for customer updates.
Alex: Notes from outgoing shift (Marta): deployed a hotfix revert at 02:10, saw momentary improvement but latency climbed again around 02:40. No config changes since.
incident-bot: Incident #INC-20260314-87 created, sev=2, pages sent to @oncall. Links: https://infra.redwood/incidents/INC-20260314-87
Priya: thx Alex — I’ll stay on secondary. I'm pulling logs now and will validate slow endpoints.
Priya: quick checks I’m running: ```kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference --since=15m | egrep "ERROR|WARN"``` and perf histo: ```/ops/metrics/query?expr=latency_p99{service="inference"}```
Jordan: comms note: I'll post a brief update to #support and the affected customers doc in 15m unless we have a clearer mitigation. Will be monitoring for impact.
Alex: Runbook pointer: see internal runbook -> https://runbooks.redwood/latency-spike. Key steps 1-3: 1) check traffic shaping/alpha routes, 2) validate model shard placement, 3) fallback to lower-capacity variant.
Marta: add: check KV cache eviction — we saw cache thrashing last time which correlates with large batch sizes. Command: ```curl -s http://inference-metrics/local/cache | jq .evictions_last_min```
Priya: found spike in long-tail requests to /v1/generate with seq_len>2048. Possible batching mutation. Looking at recent routing rules...
Priya: config diff (last 24h): ```/configs/routing.yaml  +batch_timeout: 20ms  -batch_timeout: 10ms``` — that could increase batching delay under certain patterns.
Alex: Action plan for night: 1) Priya to revert batch_timeout to 10ms if we confirm correlation. 2) Jordan to post interim customer note and set expectation we’re investigating perf. 3) I’ll keep paging rotation and escalate to SRE if revert doesn't improve in 20m.
Jordan: prepping update now: "We are aware of increased latency impacting generation requests. Our on-call engineers are investigating; mitigation attempts underway. Will update in 15 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Priya: rolling back batch_timeout -> 10ms now (applying to canary first). ```kubectl apply -f /configs/routing.yaml --record```
incident-bot: Page sent to SRE-lead-Jordan per escalation policy after 20m without improvement.
Alex: If rollback improves metrics, we’ll schedule a follow-up postmortem and track as regression with routing changes. If not, we escalate to model-serving infra team and consider temporary routing to the lower-cost variant (fallback model).
Jordan: I’m watching support channel. No major customer complaints yet besides a handful of increased latencies. Will update after metrics reflect rollback.
Marta: FYI — I’ve added a short checklist to the incident ticket for whoever picks up next shift (pin: fallback model ID, contact list, and follow-up evals).
Alex: ok team, I’m staying on for the first 30m of the night. Priya you’re secondary, Jordan comms. If any gap in coverage happens (e.g., if I drop off), @Priya take leadership and tell Jordan to escalate.
Priya: acknowledged, standing by.
Jordan: acknowledged, will post updates and escalate to account team if any customer reports come in.
Alex: thanks — handoff complete. Leaving a final pointer: if you need immediate infra access creds: use ssh jump via `bastion-night` and run `sudo -i` (audit logs will capture actions).
Priya: copying runbook and commands into the ticket now.
Jordan: will post a 15min update in 5m. :thumbsup:
